content:
Redwood Inference — Compliance & Security One‑Pagers Pack (v2)
FINAL — Customer‑Facing (for security review)

Audience: Security / GRC / IT / Procurement
Deployment modes covered: Hosted API | Dedicated Capacity | Private (VPC / on‑prem)

IMPORTANT NOTES
- This pack is intended to support security review and questionnaire responses. It is not a contract and does not modify any agreement.
- Capabilities vary by deployment mode. See the “Deployment mode notes” boxes on each page.
- For requests for formal evidence (SOC 2 report, pen test summary, etc.), use the evidence request process described below.

Evidence requests / security contact
- Primary contact: security@redwoodinference.com
- Sales/Solutions Engineering can help route requests; evidence is typically shared under NDA where required.

Document control
- Version: v2.0
- Last reviewed: 2026-02-21
- Owners: Security & Compliance (Naomi Feldman, Olga Petrov) + Product Security (Marcus Lin)
- Distribution: Customer‑facing

------------------------------------------------------------
ONE‑PAGER 1/7 — Compliance Program & SOC 2 Posture
------------------------------------------------------------
Summary
Redwood Inference maintains a security and compliance program designed for production enterprise workloads. We undergo independent assessment and maintain documented policies, procedures, and technical controls aligned with common enterprise requirements.

Highlights
- Independent assurance: SOC 2 report available upon request (under NDA where applicable).
- Security governance: security policies, risk management, and annual security training.
- Secure SDLC: code review, CI controls, dependency scanning, and vulnerability management.
- Incident management: documented incident response process with customer communications governed by contract.

SOC 2 (overview)
- Report type: SOC 2 (Type II)
- Scope: Redwood Inference production systems supporting customer workloads (scope details provided in report)
- Trust Services Criteria: Security; additional criteria may be included depending on report period

Evidence available (via request)
- SOC 2 report (under NDA as required)
- SOC 2 bridge / cover letter (as available)
- Summary of independent penetration test results (high‑level)
- Security policies (select customer-facing summaries)

Deployment mode notes
- Hosted API: Covered by Redwood’s operational controls for the hosted service.
- Dedicated Capacity: Same core platform controls; adds customer-specific isolation at the infrastructure level. Contractual terms may differ.
- Private (VPC/on‑prem): Shared responsibility model applies; Redwood provides the software and defined support boundaries, while the customer controls their environment (network, host hardening, and operational processes as applicable).

Where to ask / next step
- Ask your Redwood account team to initiate an evidence request or email security@redwoodinference.com.

Footer: Redwood Inference | Compliance & Security One‑Pagers Pack v2.0 | Last reviewed 2026-02-21

------------------------------------------------------------
ONE‑PAGER 2/7 — Encryption & Key Management
------------------------------------------------------------
Summary
Redwood Inference is designed to protect customer data in transit and at rest using industry-standard encryption mechanisms. Key management options vary by deployment mode.

In transit
- TLS is used for communications between clients and Redwood endpoints.
- Recommended: customers enforce modern TLS configurations and standard certificate validation in their clients.

At rest
- Data stored by Redwood for service operation is encrypted at rest using cloud-provider supported encryption mechanisms.
- Backups/snapshots (where used) inherit at-rest encryption controls.

Key management
- Hosted API / Dedicated Capacity:
  - Encryption keys are managed via Redwood’s cloud key management systems (KMS).
  - Access to keys is restricted and audited.
- Private (VPC/on‑prem):
  - Customers may integrate with their own KMS/HSM and key rotation policies depending on deployment architecture.
  - The specific integration approach is documented during deployment design.

What data is encrypted?
- Customer traffic to the service (in transit)
- Service operational data stored for platform functionality (at rest)

Notes on “customer prompts and outputs”
- Redwood’s standard service operation may require transient processing of prompts/outputs to generate responses.
- Data retention and logging behavior varies by configuration and deployment mode; see the Data Retention & Deletion one‑pager.

Deployment mode notes
- Hosted API: Redwood manages the full stack for encryption controls.
- Dedicated Capacity: Redwood manages encryption controls for the dedicated environment; customers can request additional configuration options depending on contract.
- Private: Customers control the environment and can enforce organization-specific encryption and key policies.

Footer: Redwood Inference | Compliance & Security One‑Pagers Pack v2.0 | Last reviewed 2026-02-21

------------------------------------------------------------
ONE‑PAGER 3/7 — Identity, SSO (SAML), SCIM & RBAC
------------------------------------------------------------
Summary
Redwood supports enterprise identity controls for authenticating users and administering access to the Redwood Console and associated resources.

SSO / SAML
- Supports SSO via SAML for Redwood Console access (enterprise plans).
- Common IdP integrations: Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace (via SAML).

SCIM (provisioning)
- SCIM support may be available depending on plan and deployment mode.
- If SCIM is not enabled for your plan, Redwood supports administrative user management and standard SSO enforcement.

RBAC (role-based access control)
- Role-based access controls are available to support least privilege.
- Recommended pattern:
  - Restrict “Admin” roles to a small set of platform owners.
  - Use separate roles for billing/usage, org settings, and operational activities.

API keys / service access
- API keys can be created and revoked by authorized users.
- Key usage can be audited via platform logs (see Audit Logging one‑pager).

Deployment mode notes
- Hosted API: SSO/RBAC applies to Redwood Console and org-level controls.
- Dedicated Capacity: Same control plane capabilities; may include additional segregation and admin boundaries by contract.
- Private: SSO/RBAC may integrate with customer identity systems; specific approach depends on deployment topology.

Customer responsibilities (shared responsibility)
- Configure SSO enforcement and user lifecycle policies (e.g., MFA at IdP, offboarding SLAs).
- Maintain least privilege assignments and periodic access reviews.

Footer: Redwood Inference | Compliance & Security One‑Pagers Pack v2.0 | Last reviewed 2026-02-21

------------------------------------------------------------
ONE‑PAGER 4/7 — Audit Logging & Monitoring
------------------------------------------------------------
Summary
Redwood provides audit logging to support traceability of administrative actions and security-relevant events. Log coverage varies by feature and deployment mode.

What is typically logged (examples)
- Identity & access events: user sign-ins, SSO configuration changes, role changes
- Organization/admin events: API key creation/revocation, permission changes
- Operational events (platform): select configuration and deployment events where applicable

What audit logs are designed for
- Security investigations and compliance evidence
- Administrative accountability
- Change management traceability

Export / access
- Audit logs are available via the Redwood Console.
- Export mechanisms (e.g., API access or forwarding to a SIEM) may be available depending on plan and deployment mode.

Data minimization
- Audit logs are designed to capture security-relevant metadata. Content logging of prompts/outputs is not required for auditability and is governed separately (see Data Retention & Deletion).

Deployment mode notes
- Hosted API: Redwood provides standard audit log access; export options may be plan-dependent.
- Dedicated Capacity: Additional integration options may be available for enterprise needs (e.g., SIEM forwarding) depending on architecture.
- Private: Audit logging and export are typically integrated with customer logging/monitoring stack; responsibilities are shared.

Customer responsibilities (recommended)
- Define retention requirements for audit logs (per policy/regulation).
- Route logs to your central logging/SIEM if required.
- Restrict access to audit logs to authorized personnel.

Footer: Redwood Inference | Compliance & Security One‑Pagers Pack v2.0 | Last reviewed 2026-02-21

------------------------------------------------------------
ONE‑PAGER 5/7 — Data Residency (Regions) & Data Flows
------------------------------------------------------------
Summary
Redwood supports regional deployment options and data residency expectations. Available regions and residency guarantees depend on the selected deployment mode and contracted scope.

Hosted API (regional controls)
- Workloads can be served from supported cloud regions.
- Region availability may change as Redwood expands; your account team can confirm current supported regions for production.

Dedicated Capacity
- Dedicated environments can be provisioned in agreed regions (subject to hardware availability).
- Dedicated is often used to meet data isolation and residency objectives.

Private (VPC / on‑prem)
- Private deployment enables customers to run the Redwood control/data plane components within a customer-controlled environment.
- This mode is typically used for strict data residency, regulated workloads, or customer-managed networking requirements.

Telemetry and service operations
- Redwood uses operational telemetry for reliability and support. The scope of telemetry and where it is processed depends on deployment mode and configuration.
- Customers can discuss additional constraints (e.g., telemetry minimization, routing restrictions) during security review and deployment design.

Shared responsibility reminder
- Residency outcomes depend on how the customer configures routing, networking controls, and any customer-managed integrations.

Footer: Redwood Inference | Compliance & Security One‑Pagers Pack v2.0 | Last reviewed 2026-02-21

------------------------------------------------------------
ONE‑PAGER 6/7 — Data Retention, Deletion & Customer Controls
------------------------------------------------------------
Summary
Redwood is designed to minimize data retention while supporting reliable service operations. Retention controls vary by data type and deployment mode.

Key concepts
- Processing vs. storage: prompts/outputs are processed to generate responses; storage (if any) is governed by product configuration and support needs.
- Operational logs (e.g., audit logs, system logs) are retained for security, reliability, and support.

Retention (high-level)
- Hosted API:
  - Retention defaults apply to operational logs.
  - Extended retention for certain logs may be available as an enterprise option.
  - Customer content retention (if enabled for a feature) is configured and documented; ask your account team for current behavior for your plan.
- Dedicated Capacity:
  - Retention can often be tailored to enterprise requirements subject to technical constraints.
- Private (VPC/on‑prem):
  - Customers typically control retention directly within their environment and can align retention to internal policy.

Deletion requests
- Customers may request deletion of customer data in accordance with the applicable agreement and product behavior.
- Deletion workflows and timelines can vary based on deployment mode, data type, and contractual commitments.

What we recommend customers do
- Define internal retention requirements for: audit logs, access logs, and any application-level logs that may contain prompts/outputs.
- Use least-privilege access to logs and restrict export destinations.
- Document your chosen configuration for compliance audits.

Footer: Redwood Inference | Compliance & Security One‑Pagers Pack v2.0 | Last reviewed 2026-02-21

------------------------------------------------------------
ONE‑PAGER 7/7 — Subprocessors & Vendor Management (Customer-Facing Overview)
------------------------------------------------------------
Summary
Redwood uses a limited set of subprocessors and vendors to deliver and support the service (e.g., cloud infrastructure, monitoring, customer support tooling). Redwood reviews vendors for security risk and maintains vendor management practices aligned with our compliance program.

What we provide
- A current subprocessor list (customer-facing) and update process where applicable.
- Information needed for DPA/vendor due diligence workflows, subject to confidentiality.

How to request
- Request the latest subprocessor list from your Redwood account team or security@redwoodinference.com.
- Some details may require an NDA depending on the content requested.

Deployment mode notes
- Hosted API / Dedicated Capacity: Redwood’s vendor set includes infrastructure and operational tooling used to run the service.
- Private: Vendor/subprocessor scope changes because the customer operates the environment; Redwood’s list primarily relates to support, updates, and (optionally) telemetry.

Footer: Redwood Inference | Compliance & Security One‑Pagers Pack v2.0 | Last reviewed 2026-02-21

------------------------------------------------------------
Appendix (field guidance — remove if customer requests “strictly one‑pagers only”)
------------------------------------------------------------
If a prospect requests:
- “SOC 2 report”: route to GRC (evidence request) and confirm NDA status.
- “Pen test report”: offer the approved high-level summary first; full reports are shared selectively.
- “Data retention in days”: confirm exact retention by log type and plan before committing in writing.
- “Private deployment boundary”: offer a technical deep dive with Solutions Engineering to map responsibilities.

End of pack.
